description: Sample Itihāsa corpus — starter verses from Rāmāyaṇa and Mahābhārata

verses.iast: tapaḥsvādhyāyanirataṃ tapasvī vāgvidāṃ varam | nāradaṃ paripapraccha vālmīkir munisattamam
verses.gloss: The ascetic Vālmīki, devoted to austerity and study, asked Nārada, the best of sages and eloquent speaker.

verses.iast: ko nv asmin sāmprataṃ loke guṇavān kaś ca vīryavān | dharmajñaś ca kṛtajñaś ca satyavākyo dṛḍhavrataḥ
verses.gloss: Who in this world today is virtuous, valiant, knowing dharma, grateful, truthful, and firm in vows?

verses.iast: kāvyam ity eva tasyāsīt tapasā brahmaṇā samam | kāvyasya karaṇād dhīmān saṃpannaḥ kavipuṅgavaḥ
verses.gloss: Through his austerity, his poetry became equal to Brahman. Through composing poetry, the wise one became the foremost of poets.

verses.iast: nārāyaṇaṃ namaskṛtya naraṃ caiva narottamam | devīṃ sarasvatīṃ caiva tato jayam udīrayet
verses.gloss: Having bowed to Nārāyaṇa and Nara (the best of men), and to the goddess Sarasvatī, one should declare victory.

verses.iast: lomaharṣaṇaputra ugraśravāḥ sūtaḥ paurāṇiko naimiṣāraṇyake | śaunakaṃ kulapatiṃ abhyagacchat
verses.gloss: Ugraśravā, the son of Lomaharṣaṇa, a bard learned in the Purāṇas, came to the forest of Naimiṣa to the head of the family, Śaunaka.

verses.iast: karmaṇy evādhikāras te mā phaleṣu kadācana | mā karmaphalahetur bhūr mā te saṅgo 'stv akarmaṇi
verses.gloss: You have a right only to action, never to its fruits. Do not be the cause of the fruits of action. Do not be attached to inaction.

verses.iast: yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānir bhavati bhārata | abhyutthānam adharmasya tadātmānaṃ sṛjāmy aham
verses.gloss: Whenever there is a decline of dharma and a rise of adharma, O Bhārata, then I manifest myself.

verses.iast: paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṃ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām | dharmasaṃsthāpanārthāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge
verses.gloss: For the protection of the good, for the destruction of the wicked, and for the establishment of dharma, I am born age after age.

verses.iast: sarvadharmān parityajya mām ekaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja | ahaṃ tvāṃ sarvapāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ
verses.gloss: Abandoning all dharmas, take refuge in me alone. I will liberate you from all sins. Do not grieve.

verses.iast: rāmo rāmo rāma iti prajānām abhavan kathāḥ | rāme rājyaṃ praśāsati
verses.gloss: During Rāma's reign, 'Rāma, Rāma, Rāma' became the constant talk of the people.
